summary: Iteration 30 — PII masking + audited super-admin reveal / temp-password + bleach-sanitised rich-text HTML across every dynamic content field. New pytest module /app/backend/tests/test_iteration30_pii_richtext.py — 24/24 PASS covering: (a) GET /api/admin/users returns masked email/mobile with pii_masked=true; can_reveal=true only for team:manage. A synthetic staff user with the 'support' preset (members:view but not team:manage) sees masked values with can_reveal=false; ops.manager legacy perms have no members:view and get 403 (as-is). Partner gets 403. (b) POST /api/admin/users/{uid}/reveal returns real values + seconds=10 for super admin, 403 for manager/partner/member, 400 for bad ObjectId, 404 for unknown id; audit row user.pii_reveal written per call. (c) POST /api/admin/users/{uid}/temp-password rotates bcrypt hash, sets must_change_password=true + password_reset_by/at, old password stops working (401), new one logs in, audit row user.temp_password written; teardown restores original hash and (if the pre-test hash was already stale) reseeds User@123 so downstream suites keep passing. (d) reject_masked() blocks PUT /api/admin/users/{uid} when email or mobile contains •, and real values save. (e) bleach.safe_html strips
action_items: Optional: reveal_user_pii + issue_temp_password enforce require_perm('team:manage') so a legacy 'admin' role user without staff_role still works, but a support-preset staff user with members:view+no team:manage rightly gets 403. The review request's phrasing ('Super admin can view and manage the access') matches. No fix needed.
Optional: /api/admin/users pagination doesn't include the temp staff user unless created_at is present — my TestPiiMasking.test_staff_with_members_view_only injects created_at explicitly to be safe.

Optional: consider adding an idempotency guard on /admin/users/{uid}/temp-password so a rapid double-click doesn't rotate the password twice within the 10s window (currently every call mints a new one and audits both).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2497 masked_user() mutates the input dict in place; admin_users() calls clean(d) first so it's safe, but if masked_user is ever used on a raw motor doc it would leak _id via mutation.

server.py:2528 reveal_user_pii returns email + mobile in plain JSON with no rate-limit — a compromised super-admin session can enumerate every account. Consider a per-actor sliding window (e.g. 30 reveals/hour) with a 429 above that.

server.py:2551 temp password generation is secrets.token_urlsafe(9) + 'aA1!' — always ends in the same 4 chars. That's cosmetic (still 12 bytes of entropy from token_urlsafe) but pattern-guessable. Prefer secrets.choice() from a pool that guarantees the four character classes without a fixed suffix.

server.py:2565 reject_masked only checks the bullet char • — a client that saves with any other mask character wouldn't be caught. Acceptable because the mask is generated by the same backend, but worth a comment.

server.py:5140 safe_html() has no size cap of its own — callers all clamp with [:20000] / [:4000] / [:6000] which is good, but a single-line comment on safe_html itself would prevent a future caller from forgetting.

server.py:5171 clean_blocks() applies safe_html only to richtext/html/text/quote/cta/faq block types — 'image', 'video', 'divider', 'columns' block text (if any) skips sanitisation. Verify no block type stores untrusted HTML outside those six.

server.py:5377 admin_edit_profile uses PATCH-style body: dict rather than the AdminProfileIn model, so unlike POST it silently ignores unknown fields and cannot validate types. It still calls reject_masked + safe_html on bio which is the important bit.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the PII UI testids verified: user-email-<id>/user-mobile-<id> masked, reveal-<id> + reveal-timer-<id> countdown + re-mask after 10s, show-password-<id> present for super admin, all hidden for manager. profile-bio editor + toolbar buttons render. Discover cards emit plain text (no raw HTML).
